label: Differential error formula
subgoals: Treat dx as the measurement error
Read f'(x) as the amplification factor

slice.rule: An error $\Delta x$ in a measured input passes through $y = f(x)$ as $\Delta y \approx f'(x)\,\Delta x$: the differential $dy = f'(x)\,dx$ evaluated at the error. The derivative is the amplification factor.
For $y = \sqrt{x}$, $f'(x) = \dfrac{1}{2\sqrt{x}}$ is small when $x$ is large, so a root function shrinks the input error.

label: Reciprocal errors
subgoals: Take absolute value for the error size

slice.rule: For $y = 1/x$, $f'(x) = -1/x^2$; the size of the output error is $|\Delta y| \approx \Delta x / x^2$, which blows up for small $x$. Relative errors are cleaner: $\dfrac{\Delta y}{y} \approx \dfrac{x f'(x)}{f(x)} \cdot \dfrac{\Delta x}{x}$.

examples.says: $|\Delta y| \approx 0.01/0.01 = 1$, a 10% error in $x$ becomes 10% in $y$ but on a value of 10

slice.note: The minus sign says the output moves the other way; the error size is the absolute value.
